cells.tense: Something is moving toward you and you can feel it arriving before it has a shape.
cells.ask: Say out loud to yourself what you hope to hear from someone. Then leave a little room in that conversation for it to arrive your way.
cells.core: You can feel things coming before they have a shape. You're open to what's next, and the news lands in your body faster than it lands in words. Some of what arrives gets weighed right away, measured against what you already know. The fresh part is how much of yourself you leave open when someone tells you something you didn't predict. If you're already sorting while they talk, you get the version you prepared for. If you hold off, you get them. Both can happen in one conversation — you don't have to choose between being sharp and being reachable. If something falls out of your week, this is what drops first. One small return will be enough to keep it alive. You've already got the door open. You just have to stop rushing what comes through it.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it coming before it has a shape.
cells.verb: opening to feel what's here before knowing what it is
cells.place: standing in the middle of the pattern you can see whole

cells.tense: You reach for what every exchange might become before any of them have actually happened.
cells.ask: Pick one conversation and go in with no outcome in mind. Say only what's true now; let what comes back land before you answer it.
cells.core: You reach into every exchange for what it might become. A friend starts a sentence and you're already feeling where it could lead, already holding its possible versions, already preparing for the ones you want. You're open, maybe more open than the people around you. But planning what hasn't arrived keeps you in a future you can't live in. The whole picture is true and it isn't finished — seeing it doesn't need a last answer to be real. It can keep changing as more comes in. If the ending you've been bracing for doesn't arrive, the people beside you still felt the wait: the pause before they'd put down what they came to say. This isn't about staying calm. It's about the one move you make that points somewhere real.
cells.sheetLine: You see how it could go before it has gone anywhere.

cells.tense: The door was open at some earlier point, and you have been standing on the far side of it since then.
cells.ask: Let one person finish a story tomorrow without preparing your answer while they talk. Listen for one thing you didn't already know.
cells.core: The receiving part of you went quiet, and it went quiet a while back. It isn't that you don't feel things now. It's that the door stays shut and you stopped noticing the shutness — news lands, and somewhere in you it gets filed before it gets felt. Emotion isn't the absent piece. What's absent is the moment before the filing: something arriving with no opinion waiting for it. That's what seeing the whole shape of things runs on — the fresh part of any exchange is the person showing up differently than you expected. When you're managing what comes in, you only get the versions you already saw. You're not empty, and that isn't the claim. It's that one thing could stay open a few seconds longer than you usually let it.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the door shut without noticing your hand on it.

cells.tense: You decided what each exchange was worth a long time ago, and you stopped noticing you decided.
cells.ask: With one person you're close to, name something they gave you recently — say it plain, out loud, without adding a favor back.
cells.core: You've been keeping quiet accounts with the people near you. Not coldly — it happens on its own, like breathing. You give, you notice what comes back, you adjust, and you call none of it a decision. But the accounts run quiet and steady, and you run on them. What you're not seeing is that you set these terms. You decided how much to offer, how much to hold back, what someone has to do to earn your openness. Seeing the whole pattern includes the pattern you're in. Saying the terms out loud is the step. It doesn't undo the fairness — it makes the fairness true between you instead of something you're running alone. Looking honestly at your own accounts, you'd find something like this, one person at a time. You can too.
cells.sheetLine: You set fair terms with people and call them the facts.

attempts.check: The record has the Balance face present and open to receive; it does not say what part of life this is, whether a specific opening is happening now, or that the person would recognize themselves in it. The reader could reasonably say: some weeks this is exactly me, some weeks it's flat. The ask stands on its own either way; it is one step toward more exchange and does not depend on the reading being true. The sentence that serves this house more than the person: 'trust what you're receiving' — it sounds like me, but it asks for a feeling, not something I can do.
